Hypercasual Teardown · Mobile web adaptation · 06 October 2026

Pull Him Out

The hazard is the tool. A comic rescue puzzle turns the order of a few pin pulls into a chain of dangerous, useful consequences.

A treasure hunter is trapped inside a tiny machine. Gold, lava, water and enemies wait on separate shelves. The player’s job is to decide which things should meet—and which must stay apart until the room is safe.

Analytical reference: Lion Studios’ mobile game.
Target: a complete, original mobile web adaptation for bug.games.
This document is the specification; no game has been built or published.

01 / The decision that carries the game

Change the room before you free the hero

The important action is small: release a barrier. Its meaning is large because it changes contact. Water can turn an exposed lava basin into a traversable surface; that same lava can dispose of a hostile actor first. Releasing the treasure too early can lose the objective while the explorer is still alive.

Most of the thinking happens before commitment. There is no evidence of a conventional combat kit or a health economy in these scenes. The player does not steer the explorer through danger; opening the environment lets actors and materials resolve the next part of the puzzle. This makes order, separation and destination more useful design concepts than reflex speed.

A readable toy with an irreversible question

Bold silhouettes and contrasting liquids make the initial state understandable at a glance. Gold pins are both the interface and the architecture. The opening hand points to one safe action; later rooms retain the same visual grammar while adding another consequence to predict.

The pin feels powerful because it releases something already visible. Good rooms promise a result before the pull, show the contact after it, and leave a stable new state the player can reason about. Particles are pleasurable evidence of change, but the remaining barrier, living actor and safe surface carry the actual rule.

The load-bearing chain

ReadLocate the hero, objective, hazards and barriers.
Choose contactWhich material or actor should reach which destination first?
Commit a pullThe opened channel changes the room; the actor moves automatically.
ReassessUse the new safe state, or retry with a different order.

Interpretation from the reviewed rooms: escalation works by recombining known relationships, then changing the objective. This is not proof that every level uses the same number of pins, failure rule or movement trigger.

02 / Characteristic episode · EP-01

Gold first loses. Danger first can win.

The Level 7 layout contains water above, treasure held to the left, lava held to the right and a zombie below. There is no boulder in this room. The sampled failed attempt releases the coins toward active lava. A later attempt changes the lower hazard state before opening the treasure route.

What is actually established. The reviewed states show a failed objective route, reset, hazard conversion and safe collection phase. The precise pin inputs between samples are inferred from changed barriers; the video’s five-second seek steps do not measure animation duration or input latency. The exact defeat trigger is not continuously sampled. In the target, loss of the required treasure is explicitly a failure reason.

Dependency, not a memorised hand motion

Lava → enemyUse a dangerous material while the treasure remains isolated.
Water → lavaChange the traversed area into a safe support.
Open the routeRelease the objective only after its destination is safe.
Hero → objectiveAutomatic movement completes the planned chain.

This sequence is a target acceptance chain supported by the source states, with its input order partly inferred. It makes the game’s central reversal concrete: a hazard is useful until the wrong thing touches it. A retry should teach that relationship, rather than merely announce that the player was wrong.

03 / Rules, combinations and boundaries

Do not turn an example into a universal law

Water and lava can create rock in the contacted region. This is stronger than a purely cosmetic splash and narrower than “one drop of water neutralises all lava.” The visible residue matters: a builder should conserve readable safe and unsafe regions rather than globally flip a hazard off.

04 / Progression through changed situations

The same verb survives five worlds

The recordings move from tomb treasure to urban escape, island survival, an underwater ritual and an arena relic. Their shared logic survives the change of scenery: isolate a threat, redirect a material, open a safe route, collect the thing needed to continue. Narrative fetch objectives give this otherwise compact puzzle system a longer direction.

Tomb → city: learn a relationship, then meet an exception

The tomb establishes gravity, treasure and hot/cold contact. The city adds things the same bright pin cannot explain on its own: live electricity, protective equipment, gas and a hungry dog. These require a preparation state that is distinguishable from “safe to walk now.” A mask should be legible on the actor, not hidden in a reward pop-up.

Three key silhouettes appear in the HUD, but they do not establish the exact schedule of key awards or whether every chapter uses them identically. The reports describe crystal, companion and passport objectives; sampled frames do not certify their complete acquisition sequence.

Island: manufacture a route and gather a kit

Logs, matches, food, carts and heavy objects shift the fantasy from fetching treasure to assembling an escape. A spike pit can become a crossing if a correctly placed object creates support. Carts introduce moving consequences: route and impact direction matter as much as release order. The visible cart scene contains one downed boar and another living one; it does not prove a simultaneous multi-enemy crush.

Undersea: change the objective and the available helpers

The explorer’s translucent aquatic presentation and a tentacle introduce a new grammar of allies and threats. The ritual scene visibly asks for a boot, fish skeleton and food can. Those odd items make completion comic and concrete. The exact eel range, tentacle activation condition and earlier gate-offering sequence are not sampled; the target must author these relationships rather than quietly omit them.

Arena: combine actor priority with a three-part climax

The arena returns hard edges and hostile actors. In the inspected knight scene the dog is already down, the knight is still standing and the rock is airborne. The desired rescue remains distinct from enemy-versus-enemy resolution. The held glove shows three coloured inlays; literal franchise names and lore are not needed to explain its structural role as a collected three-part objective.

Additional browser inspection shows the explorer travelling through a portal and then back on a domestic sofa. This supports a return-home beat after the relic scene. A full interactive vampire chapter is not established; the reported continuation remains outside the reviewed puzzle inventory.

The independently checked key trial adds a different causal tool: an armed horizontal launcher. The before/after states distinguish projectile defeat from a boulder crush because the rock remains held. The exact triggering input is inferred between samples; this does not establish a universal fire rate or damage rule.

05 / Reward, interruption and reasons to return

Let the result finish before selling the next action

The checked result displays +50, CLAIM 200, an x4 multiplier, NEW SKIN 25% and a 550 wallet. That is one recorded result, not a universal payout table. The failure surface displays a changing countdown and a Hint control with a film icon. These layers can interrupt the short causal lesson that just happened.

The museum gives saved progress somewhere to live; cosmetics let rewards change appearance without changing the pin puzzle. Exact purchase prices, exhibit unlock order, visitor payments and skin thresholds are not verified in this packet. None should be inferred from empty display cases or a partially covered offer.

A good retry preserves the question and explains the failed contact. A good reward gives the solved room a clean ending.

Short game-specific Build prompt

Build the complete mobile web adaptation of Pull Him Out described here: a comic expedition where one thumb releases pins to decide which hazards, helpers and treasures meet, while the explorer moves automatically. Deliver all five worlds, their connected objectives, museum and replay through a satisfying return home as one portable HTML with original art and full sound. Use portrait tap-to-pull and the short-session bridge in #adaptation-bridge. Preserve #core-statements and EP-01’s danger → cooling → safe treasure chain; follow #build-rules, design the open parts in #design-space, and develop the first 20 minutes from #roblox-hooks. Include EN/RU settings, independent music/SFX levels, and #bug-games-plan. Extract and inspect the required images, then plan, build, play-test and fix the entire game. Report design choices and actual coverage; an opening demo does not fulfil this scope.

Read this file before implementation

  1. Parse all static text, tables and expanded or collapsed sections without dumping base64 into the text context.
  2. Extract every image in the evidence index; match its required figure ID and inspect it with an image tool. Check the visible actor, barrier and material states against the associated rule. If your environment cannot view images, state that limitation rather than claiming inspection.
  3. Read the complete scope, core, bridge, design space, assets, audio, integration and frozen acceptance cases together. The screenshots are analytical references, not licensed game assets.
  4. Build and test the whole connected game in this task. Internal milestones may organise work but do not reduce delivery. Save notable choices and revise designed expectations transparently when those choices change.

These are Designed prices, reviewed as a complete attainable free collection rather than copied source prices. Finishes change presentation only; the artifact itself is earned by chapter completion. No purchase grants keys, required items, immunity, hints or an easier pin order. Keys and kit items are world-scoped, visibly obtained in rooms, consumed/marked complete at their chapter gate, and never sold. Coins are committed once on the settled result, so retry/reload cannot double-award. There is one explorer with chapter equipment states and a companion objective; no class or combat-build alternatives.

Save/continue. Save a schema version, cleared-room set, next room, world items, unique reward claims, coin ledger, acquired/selected cosmetics and museum finishes. Save after each clear and cosmetic transaction. Resume a partially played room at its initial state; do not serialize unsettled fluid physics. “Retry” resets the current attempt only. Guard storage failures and retain a playable unsaved session with a concise translated notice. Keep EN/RU and both volume values as separate device preferences; validate migrations and never confuse failed load with an empty new save.

Principles for authoring the remaining rooms

  • Predictable contact, surprising use. Show all consequential destinations before commitment; novelty comes from recombination, not changing a familiar material’s rule without warning.
  • Teach through a changed state. One safe pull demonstrates the relationship. The next room asks an independent choice, then a later room combines it with a previous relationship.
  • Escalate dependencies. Add a preparation step, a second vulnerable owner or a route that helps one actor and threatens another. More pins alone do not guarantee more reasoning.
  • Reward completion with meaning. The hero, objective and room should resolve clearly before the next screen. Chapter objects visibly build the escape; the museum records it.
  • Keep retries about hypotheses. Restore the same readable initial state, identify the failed contact, and let the next attempt begin immediately. Never replace learning with a percentile claim.

Round states and mobile input · Designed

Entry into the current room → first meaningful touch → pin preparation/highlight → committed opening → continuous fluid/object/actor resolution → stable new choice → clear or cause-specific failure → Next or same-room Retry. Pause and Settings suspend the simulation without discarding the attempt. Typical target room effort is about 20–90 seconds including thought; this is a tuning intention, not a measured source duration. Campaign difficulty increases in dependencies and actor context. Keys, artifacts, coins and clear flags persist; physical consequences reset on retry.

Action / stateResult and edge behaviour
Short tap on a removable handlePointer-down highlights the handle. Pointer-up inside its 44–56 CSS-pixel target commits one pull. Move out or pointercancel cancels without consequence. Collision silhouette remains narrower than the hit target; neighbouring targets must not overlap ambiguously.
Hold / dragHolding reveals handle axis and name without a hover dependency. A rail pin slides only along its shown axis and snaps at authored stops; returning before release cancels. No hidden global swipe gesture or joystick.
Outside / repeated touchOutside touch clears highlight. A second pointer is ignored for commitment; use one tracked pointer ID. Duplicate tap/release events cannot remove a second pin. No queued input may fire after a room transitions.
ResolutionPins required for a timed combination remain usable when their future state is readable; disable only consumed/blocked handles. Never globally freeze a multi-step puzzle until every particle sleeps. Show local readiness, not invisible cooldown.
Portrait, thumb, rotationFrame the entire decision chamber above a lower safe-area control band. HUD and feedback cannot cover threat paths; do not require fullscreen. Letterbox/reflow on rotation, preserve attempt and pause during resize; no mandatory orientation lock or vibration.
Pause, focus loss, browser embeddingSettings and pause stop physics and mute output. Hidden/sign-in/platform pause also stop. Resume does not apply elapsed hidden time or override a user pause. Tap resumed play deliberately when user-paused.
Result, Retry and informationA cause marker points to the contact/objective before the translated reason. Retry restores the same room in one touch with prior progress intact. Free hints and optional cosmetic information have Back/Close; leaving them never purchases or commits a pin.

Original art, with the same decision signals

Designed look: a warm, hand-drawn expedition comic with crisp outlined characters, chunky metal handles, readable translucent fluids and five coherent material palettes. Keep the source’s treasure-hunter fantasy, danger silhouettes and before/after grammar; replace its art, franchise references and costumes with original characters and a three-part compass relic. A fixed portrait chamber shows the complete relevant routes at choice time; the thumb and compact HUD sit outside them. Telegraph a heavy release, make contact decisive, then let the new stable state be seen before a large celebration. Effects support the object, owner and outcome.

Bloom Brain: one bounded teaching transfer

The bundled read-only locator found the local Bloom Brain archive at ~/.bloom-brain/knowledge (619 pages); the absence of an MCP search tool did not stop the check. Keyword search ran without tag filters or semantic credentials. Queries: pull pins rescue puzzle traps order first action clear failure retry; puzzle escape button sequence lever traps first touch feedback retry checkpoint; pull pin puzzle escape lever trap checkpoint. Selected pages’ teaching, loop, feedback and takeaways were read. Their original recordings were not newly replayed; this is checked secondary documentation, not measured retention evidence.

Problem / donorTechnique and transferRisk / before-after hypothesis / test
H01 · Unclear relation between a tiny gesture and automatic movement+1 Tongue Escape, artifacts/pages/1-tongue-escape.md, snapshot 11 Sep 2026; FTUE §3 and feel §9, EV004 (~2:22) and EV026 (~14:15). The page describes creating a route with a tongue attachment, then automatic traversal, and a visible line/crossing goal. Transfer the contextual action → route → traversal lesson via B02.Designed: one safe handle cue stays until the changed route and arrival are visible, then disappears; next room has two possible first pulls. Before: player repeats prompted taps without knowing ownership. After: player predicts how a pin changes the explorer’s route. AC01/15 asks for this prediction without a solution arrow. Do not copy tap-to-grow, training, rebirth, shop or server systems.
Failure without an actionable lesson · AI Interrogationartifacts/pages/ai-interrogation.md, snapshot 02 Sep 2026. §4 documents weak learning after failure. Checked as a negative comparison only.Rejected as a donor: dialogue/model dependency and attempt systems do not share this physical decision and do not work as the same offline loop. EP-01 itself supplies the cause-specific retry requirement.
Visible goal / recovery · The Locust’s Manorartifacts/pages/the-locust-s-manor.md, snapshot 03 Sep 2026; escape/key structure read, exact relevant lever transition not performed in that packet.Rejected: key pursuit and timed threat do not prove a transferable pin-order lesson. The current game already has visible item slots; no pursuit timer or borrowed economy is added.

H01 is a proposed teaching improvement, not proof of better engagement. It preserves offline, one-HTML delivery and the same causal choice. The build must validate the transfer through ordinary phone play.

First session checkpoints · intentions, not timer quotas

Approximate checkpointPlayer does / visible feedback / reason to continue
30 secondsMake the safe first pull, see the route and automatic collection, then meet the first independent choice. No account, title obstacle or store.
2 minutesUse water to change a hot destination; distinguish a preparatory action from opening the hero route. A failure points at its cause and Retry tests a new order.
5 minutesSolve an EP-01-style recombination and see a chapter item fill its slot. The next room offers a new relationship, not just more pins.
10 minutesComplete or approach the tomb gate, see the companion/escape beat, and optionally inspect an earned museum artifact. Slower players get useful retries rather than a scheduled unlock.
20 minutesEnter more complex city dependencies or deepen mastery in earlier rooms: protective actor state, delayed objective release, readable safe result. Continue toward the next escape objective; quit/reload returns to earned progress.

bug.games integration and analytics · Designed

Current platform SDK documentation was checked through sdk_docs on 06 Oct 2026. Core gameplay, assets, saves and settings must work offline in one portable HTML. When embedded, conditionally import the platform SDK from /sdk/bloomplay.js on the game’s own origin, then initialise with save preload and a bounded timeout; never fetch undocumented platform APIs. Standalone window.parent === window uses local services and makes no external requests. SDK failure preserves play and last-confirmed data. The platform-enabled hosted edition may request this SDK; it is the explicit exception to the standalone network-free contract.

Send loading()/loaded() around actual readiness. Call gameplayStart() on the active room and gameplayStop() on results, museum, pause and settings, only when the state changes. On late SDK connection, re-emit the present activity state. Use progress.moment(name) for ordered milestones and analytics.track(event, props) for the specific questions below. Do not duplicate automatic platform sessions, screen visibility or purchase telemetry. Treat platform pause/resume and mute as idempotent: platform mute overrides output but never rewrites saved channel preferences.

Use SDK save readiness before reading a remote save; a failed read is not a successful empty save. Merge cleared rooms/reward claims without duplicating rewards, reconcile coin transactions and cosmetic ownership, and keep device settings separate from progress. Never overwrite known progress with defaults while a load is pending. Local fallback remains playable; if reconciliation fails, retain the last confirmed state and disclose unsaved progress without losing the room.

The title is an original target working title, not a new source claim. Five minutes describes a typical intended visit, not campaign completion. Validate the current schema at build time; milestones must be reached in normal play and recorded once per save. No product is built or declared for sale in this authoring run.

Game eventExact trigger / necessary propertiesQuestion
room_attempt_startedRoom enters interactive initial state. world_id, room_id, attempt_id, attempt_number, entry_reason (new/retry/replay/resume). No personal identifiers.Where does new play stop, and which rooms need repeated attempts?
pin_committedOne recognised irreversible pull or authored rail move. attempt_id, room_id, pin_id, move_index, pin_kind.Which early decisions correlate with the losing route? No per-frame pointer telemetry.
reaction_resolvedA defined material/actor transformation becomes a stable state. attempt_id, room_id, reaction_id, affected_role, outcome. Once per reaction instance.Did players create the intended safe state before opening the objective?
room_failedFailure state first commits. attempt_id, room_id, failure_reason (hero_contact/objective_lost/blocked_goal), hazard_id, last_pin_id, elapsed_active_ms.Is loss explained by the same hazard that players report? Are objective failures being confused with hero death?
retry_selectedPlayer taps Retry on a failure result. prior_attempt_id, room_id, elapsed_since_failure_ms. New attempt gets a new ID.Do players test another hypothesis after failure?
hint_step_viewedPlayer explicitly opens a hint step. room_id, attempt_id, hint_step, hint_kind (relationship/action). No solution auto-action.Where does causal teaching fail without a hint?
room_clearedWin first commits after required collection and safe hero state. attempt_id, room_id, first_clear, move_count, elapsed_active_ms, hint_steps, earned_coins.Can players solve after learning? Separate replay from first-clear rewards.
collection_changedCommitted free museum finish/palette transaction. item_id, kind, price_coins, balance_after, transaction_id.Do earned coins have an understood destination?
language_changed / audio_preferences_changedCommitted setting change. language enum; or channel and new value/zero flag. One event on release, not slider movement.Are controls discoverable? Channel preferences are player choices, not proof audio played.

Analysis plan. Compare first-touch → first clear; attempted EP-01 paths → failure reason → retry → eventual clear; first chapter clear → museum inspection/spend; and voluntary return after a saved clear. Segment by room, new/replay entry and language, rather than comparing raw totals between different stages. Review high-failure rooms with actual contact replays and player feedback before changing physics. No numerical retention baseline or business forecast is available. The later build should verify event de-duplication and properties in SDK mock mode; production retention conclusions require real player data.

Optional Extras · none at launch; one explicitly planned idea

Extra / statusValue beyond the complete free gameDiscovery and fallback
expedition-costume · Planned, not built, not declaredOne additional original costume family; appearance only. All 42 rooms, ordinary palettes, exhibits, hints and ending remain free. No keys, score multipliers, immunity or skip.No empty shop or Buy control at launch. If built later: optional museum wardrobe, reversible preview, full plain-language effect and price before purchase; return to prior appearance on cancel.
Future completed offer onlyA real built/licensed asset family and an exact current platform price/benefit are prerequisites for product declaration/review.Query actual products and entitlements. Owned takes priority. Empty successful catalogue means no available offer; it does not prove “rejected”. Offline/failed lookup hides sale while retaining confirmed ownership. No local fake purchase success or balance authority.

If the planned extra is later completed, put only that completed review-ready product in game.json.products. Pending/rejected/unavailable/unknown states must not invite payment. Purchase cancel/failure leaves game, money display and equipment unchanged; success must be confirmed by refreshed entitlements, with one transaction result and no repeated automatic grant. Preview cannot change pin collision, actor behaviour or win rewards. An already-owned costume loads even when sales are unavailable; failed entitlement refresh retains the last confirmed ownership. An empty catalogue creates no store detour. The platform docs do not establish an ad API or revenue model, so none is assumed.

Frozen acceptance cases for the later game

These are requirements to test after implementation, not claims of an existing build. Compare the observed component against the delivered figures and the Designed component against this target contract. Record ordinary play separately from debug-staged late states.

Case / basisSetup and real inputExpected result and review
AC01 · C1/C3, B01/B02/H01 · observed setup + Designed inputFresh 390×844 portrait session, one hand, sound off. Tap the first safe handle; then play the first two-choice room without the tutorial arrow.Route opens, contents reach intended destination, explorer moves automatically. Player can identify handle, hazard and goal and predict the changed route. Thumb/HUD cannot hide the choice.
AC02 · Designed touch contractPress a handle, move outside and release; pointercancel; second pointer; double-tap during a transition; rail drag back before release.No cancelled pull, duplicate commitment or stale action in the next room. Rail stops/cancellation visible. Inspecting a pin does not spend an attempt.
AC03 · EP-01 / C2 · observed states + Inferred causeIn an EP-01-equivalent room, release required treasure before lower lava is cooled.Objective lost causes translated specific failure even with hero alive; show the coin/lava contact. Target failure trigger is Designed and distinguished from the source’s sampled sequence.
AC04 · EP-01 / R01–03Retry the same room; route lava to enemy, cool traversed area with water, then release objective and path.Stable defeated threat, visible safe support, collected objective and live explorer clear once. Restart restores all barriers/hazards, not the world’s persistent progress. Match dependency order; no source timing fidelity claim.
AC05 · R02 / local contactTest abundant lava with insufficient water and the ordinary cooling room. Release a hero path into a visibly unsafe residue.Conversion follows chosen local quantities; remaining unsafe area stays dangerous. Safe-looking rock supports actual motion; no global hidden hazard switch.
AC06 · R04–06 / Designed actor coveragePlay mass/bridge, food/dog, soap/electricity, gas/mask, cart/boar, tentacle/chef, eel and arrow/knight rooms using real inputs.Each material/actor interaction has a visible owner, trigger, result and exception. Test helper out of range, exposed vs protected hero and two concurrent contacts. Later worlds cannot be art-only reskins.
AC07 · Designed readable feelAt real speed on phone, test preparation, impact, recovery and next choice with finger, HUD and effects visible; reduced motion and sound zero.Hazard, interactive handle, protected state, new support, failure and clear remain distinct. Asset family coherent; effects do not obscure what must be predicted.
AC08 · Pause / lifecycleDuring falling liquid, open Settings, hide/reopen page, receive platform pause/resume/mute, rotate and explicitly user-pause.No hidden-time simulation jump, surprise commitment or automatic override of user pause. Output stops; saved music/SFX levels remain unchanged.
AC09 · Connected free economyComplete all rooms normally and purchase all base finishes/palettes; retry/replay/reload a clear and a transaction.42 unique clears grant 2,100 total; 2,000 buys every base item, 100 remains. No duplicate claim, negative balance or purchase gate. Exhibit artifact reflects earned chapter progress.
AC10 · Complete ordinary pathFresh save, play through all five worlds, all kits/gates, three relic trials and final home, then continue replay and collection.All 42 rooms, ending, objectives and optional collection work without store/server. Final puzzle synthesises dependencies. No later-content placeholder. Record total actual coverage and any staged states separately.
AC11 · EN/RU DesignedSwitch during an active room, failure, hint, museum and an offer-state mock; reload.All player-facing text updates, including warnings, result causes, item descriptions, errors and credits. No physics reset or clipped Russian labels; device language restored. Report prose remains English.
AC12 · Independent audio DesignedMusic to zero with effects audible, then effects zero with music audible; vary both and reload; test platform mute and first-gesture resume.Muted channel is truly silent, other level unchanged. Both preferences persist; mute overlay does not rewrite them. Listen to all integrated cues/loops, not just inspect waveform or settings.
AC13 · Save / unavailable storageReload after clear/purchase and mid-room; reject local storage; simulate remote pending/failed/empty and merge duplicate claims.Settled progress and preferences restore; in-progress room starts fresh. Unavailable storage still permits play; never erase known progress or double-award.
AC14 · SDK / optional Extra statesOffline direct-file run; embedded SDK absent/late; mock products empty/unavailable/pending/rejected, owned offline, cancel/fail/success refresh.Core always playable; no misleading Buy. Last-confirmed ownership retained; successful entitlement selects allowed cosmetic only. No duplicate session/moment/transaction events. No products at launch.
AC15 · First 20 minutes / H01Ordinary one-handed phone play from fresh save; observe checkpoints without enforcing timer unlocks.First gesture understood, independent route prediction, cause→retry learning, meaningful chapter goal and return to saved progress. Do not claim a retention improvement without players.
AC16 · Portable delivery and performanceOpen final game HTML directly in a desktop browser, then serve identical bytes over HTTPS for a real phone/iframe check. Measure size, decoded memory, first controllable frame, response and sustained frame pacing during worst fluid/effect room.All assets/fonts/audio decode with no standalone external or failed requests. Aim for responsive visible input under 100 ms and stable 60 fps on the chosen phone; report real device/results and acceptable tradeoffs. These are Designed aims, not measured guarantees. Desktop local-file support is tested separately from phone file-viewer behaviour.

Evidence readiness and remaining limits

The 24 supplied stills, raw requests, reports, source links and manifests were checked in the selected run. The acquisition helper’s short video download failed first through DNS, then timed out; the official browser player supplied discriminating Level 7 failure/retry states and late launcher trial and portal/home states. These are sampled visible states, not continuous input or audio inspection. Existing good captures were reused.

Verified geometry and contact states are sufficient to define the core adaptation. Source-accurate fluid quantities, latency, all actor interaction exceptions, full late room catalogue, exact museum economy and audio remain unverified. Current store pages are newer reception/context, not evidence of those recorded builds. The local old-teardown archive was available and checked for first-action comprehension and failure/retry clarity; no independent transfer was accepted. This does not block the complete Designed target.

Structure validation, extracted-payload checks and desktop/390×844 rendering establish document delivery only. No receiving model has yet performed an independent image-reading diagnostic, and no game fidelity, device performance, analytics delivery, sound mix or retention outcome has been tested before implementation.
